verdict.rationale: NVIDIA's DLSS docs explicitly cover the RTX 50 Series (which includes the 5090). They document DLSS Super Resolution AI upscaling and Multi Frame Generation of up to five frames per rendered frame, and say the NVIDIA app can update hundreds of games to the latest DLSS features. Tom's Hardware's hands-on review corroborates that MFG works on the card, though it notes added latency because input is sampled only at the base frame rate. Missing for 10: a concrete per-title list or count of supported games, and independent confirmation of game coverage breadth beyond NVIDIA's 'hundreds of games' claim.

support.subject: As a gamer, AI upscaling and frame generation are supported on this card — the DLSS or FSR generation is documented for this part, with broad game support

citations.quote: Powered by GeForce RTX 50 Series and fifth-generation Tensor Cores, new DLSS Multi Frame Generation boosts FPS by using AI to generate up to five frames per rendered frame.
Boosts performance by using AI to output higher-resolution frames from a lower-resolution input.

With the NVIDIA app you can update hundreds of games to use the latest DLSS features including Multi Frame Generation, and the newest AI models for DLSS Super Resolution, Frame Generation, and Ray Reconstruction.
Dynamic Multi Frame Generation maximizes smoothness by dynamically generating up to five frames per rendered frame.
